stories.headline: Karnataka | Facilitation centres to boost tourism in coastal region
stories.deck: Facilitation centres to boost tourism in coastal region
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: Karnataka's Tourism Department plans to open facilitation centres to help investors and increase tourism in the coastal region..The department is currently considering three different kinds of tourism: wellness tourism, cruise tourism and boathouse tourism to attract both local and international tourists. Wellness and boathouse tourism have been inspired by Keralam..With wellness tourism such as massages and resort spas becoming expensive, the department is also considering medium-scale spas to make them affordable to all tourists. For boathouse tourism, the department has elicited responses from interested players and received approvals from the departments concerned, a department official said..With rules and regulations from the Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority (KTCDA) and Coastal Business Zones (CBZ), approvals will be complicated and time-consuming, the officials said..This town in India is called 'Land of Seven Languages' - Can you guess it right? .Investments would require permissions from various departments and may deter some investors due to the hassles. To prevent this, the department is planning a single-window facilitation centre, one official said..Currently, cruises pass from Mumbai to Lakshadweep via Mangaluru but have not benefited the region.."A lot of the passengers do not come out and explore as they are not aware of what the region offers. So we are trying to talk them into spending one night in Mangaluru or at least providing them with enough time to explore the region," the official said..Uff, too spicy! India has a 'Chilli City' and every foodie should know it.The department is also creating a travel circuit, including adventurous water sports, in the coastal region with a mix of places to make the area attractive and easier for people planning to explore. Through this, foreign tourism is also expected to increase..Ram Prasath Manohar, Secretary of the Tourism Department, told DH: "Coastal areas are untouched opportunities for tourism. We are keeping the area's sensitivity in mind and will only prioritise sustainable materials to build properties. Land is a major bottleneck in the coastal region, hence we will have to identify its sensitivity and potential."

stories.headline: Depleting water in dams: Agriculture scenario grim in Mysuru region
stories.deck: Depleting water in dams: Agri scenario grim in Mysuru region
stories.bodyText: Mysuru: The declining water levels in the Kabini and KRS reservoirs due to the release of water to Tamil Nadu, has become a major concern among the farmers, especially paddy growers of the Mysuru region..According to the officials, the situation is grim even though the water inflow went up in last week of August following rains in Kodagu. Officials say that the water would be sufficient only to meet the drinking water needs and not for agricultural activities. Overall, Mysuru region would record less than 50% of the sowing target this year, they said..Farmers say that they would have to face worst situation in the coming months if water level in the dams go down further - after release to Tamil Nadu..The water level in the KRS dam was 107 feet on September 6. The inflow was 2,774 cusec and outflow 8,983 cusec..Cauvery water row: Several protesters briefly detained as they attempt to lay siege to KRS dam.According to K H Ravi, Joint Director, Agriculture department, Mysuru district could achieve only 44% of the sowing target this year, due to deficit rains..“The total cultivable area is around 3.82 lakh hectares, including irrigated area of around one lakh hectares (dependent on KRS and Kabini dams), and rain-fed area of around 2.7 lakh hectares. There is uncertainty this year. Even though the inflow has increased in Kabini and KRS dams, it will be sufficient only to meet the drinking water needs. Untimely rains do not help agricultural activities,” Ravi said..The officer said that there was no sufficient rain even to commence sowing in parts of Mysuru district. District in-charge Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah had strictly informed that water is released only to fill the lakes and ponds and will not be released for paddy cultivation. In Mysuru district there was a target to sow 3,76,609 hectare, but only 44.11% - 1,66,441 hectares - have been sowed, Ravi said..Mysuru region received scanty rainfall during the pre-monsoon season, which affected pre-kharif sowing and agricultural activities this year. .According to Sugarcane Growers Association president Kurubur Shanthakumar, the farmers sowing paddy are likely to suffer crop damage as the Irrigation Consultative Committee (ICC) has directed to release water only for four rotations..“Paddy is a 120-day cycle crop. The farmers will suffer loss, if the government stops releasing of water to canals,” he said..After protests by the farmers, water is being released on rotation basis from KRS dam to fill the lakes, to take up short-term crops, which are less water-intensive and to save sugarcane and other crops..More than half of Mandya district's total land area is used for agriculture, with a sowing area of 2.49 lakh hectares. The irrigated area is around 1.17 lakh hectares - KRS and Hemavathi reservoirs. The rest are dependent on tanks, wells, and borewells or rain-fed..“Deficit rains have affected sowing in Mandya district. The farmers have been strictly told not to cultivate paddy this year, following insufficient rains and less water in KRS dam. But some farmers have been involved in paddy and sugarcane cultivation. It will be difficult to release water to save the crops as the water level will deplete in the dams. This would result in loss of money spent on seeds, fertilisers and other expenses,” said G S Jayaswamy, Joint Director for Agriculture, Mandya district..In Hassan district, there was a target for sowing on 2,86,186 hectares while 93,004 hectares have been sowed. Due to deficit rains this year, the farmers of Hassan district have been suggested to cultivate ragi as an alternative crop, which requires less water, said officials.

stories.headline: Singapore must never allow prejudice against any community: PM Wong on anti-Indian abuse
stories.deck: Racist comments surfaced online targeting some of the nine Singaporeans missing in the Nepal-Tibet disaster, while questions about SIA's investment in Air India were "accompanied by anti-Indian abuse", Mr. Wong said
stories.bodyText:
Singapore must never allow prejudice against any community to become accepted or normalised, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Sunday (September 6, 2026), days after racist and xenophobic comments appeared online about the Nepal-Tibet flash floods disaster and the Singapore Airlines-Air India partnership.
"We can and should have robust debates. But we should never use seemingly legitimate arguments as a cover to fuel prejudice against any community or hostility towards foreigners," the Channel News Asia quoted Mr. Wong as saying.
The Prime Minister’s remarks come a day after Singapore Senior Minister K. Shanmugam said police are investigating “shameful” and “totally unacceptable” racist and xenophobic comments posted online about the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster and Singapore Airlines’ (SIA) investment in Air India.
In a Facebook post, Mr. Wong said that "an uglier side" had emerged in online discussions about the two matters.
Racist comments surfaced online targeting some of the nine Singaporeans missing in the Nepal-Tibet disaster, while questions about SIA's investment in Air India were "accompanied by anti-Indian abuse", he said.
While such views do not represent Singapore, they should not be dismissed as "harmless online chatter", he said.
"If such behaviour goes unchecked, it can become normalised, deepen mistrust between communities, and pull us apart," PM Wong said, adding that he had discussed the developments with his Cabinet colleagues and that this was why Mr. Shanmugam had spoken about it.
Singapore has an overall population of over six million — of which 75% are Chinese, 15% Malays, about 9% Indians and the rest from other countries.
The prosperous city-state is trying to manage a declining population due to a low local birth rate and depends on foreign talent to maintain its high-performance economic activities as part of the global network, which has already been badly hit by the West Asian conflict, a diplomatic observer said.
Mr. Wong said that Singapore had encountered similar tensions before, pointing to how “anti-foreigner” and “racial sentiments” were stirred up during the COVID-19 pandemic and surfaced during debates over the Singapore-India Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement.
Such sentiments also surfaced during the 2025 general election, when Mr. Wong spoke out against attempts to bring race and religion into politics.
"There will always be people who seek to exploit our differences," Mr. Wong said.
While it is impossible to prevent every hateful comment from appearing online, Singaporeans could choose how they respond to them, he said. "We can reject such views, and refuse to give them more space or legitimacy.” "Singapore has held together because we have consistently rejected attempts to divide us along racial or religious lines, and chosen instead to recognise one another as fellow Singaporeans," said the Prime Minister.
Former Prime Minister and now a Senior Minister in the Cabinet, Lee Hsien Loong, on Sunday (September 6) also called on Singaporeans to "stand by one another regardless of race, language or religion".
In a Facebook post, Mr. Lee described racist comments directed at the Indian community in Singapore following the recent floods in Nepal as "deeply troubling".
He added that it was "equally troubling" when issues such as SIA's investment in Air India were "distorted or exploited to stir vicious racial, anti-Indian resentment".
Expressing his condolences to those affected by the floods, Mr. Lee said the tragedy had left many families grieving and that the response should be one of "compassion and solidarity".
He also noted that Mr. Shanmugam had "laid out the issues clearly" in his statement on Saturday (September 5).
"When incidents like this happen, leaders must speak up with force and conviction, to call out what is happening, condemn the manipulation of base emotions, and call on all Singaporeans to stand together," the Channel quoted Mr. Lee as saying.

stories.headline: 'Pakistan on ventilator': Shoaib Akhtar reveals PCB’s 'nothing' expectation
stories.deck: Pakistan Cricket Board is undertaking a significant rebuilding phase following poor tour performances. Senior players have been removed from the squad for the final Test match. Former bowler Shoaib Akhtar believes the board has lost confidence in the current team. He stressed the need to protect the careers of younger fast bowlers. The board is now focusing on developing a new generation of…
stories.bodyText:
Pakistan
 cricket appears to be entering a major rebuilding phase after a disastrous start to the England tour, with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) already making significant changes before the three-Test series has even reached its conclusion.
England have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead after registering two emphatic victories. The hosts won the first Test at Headingley by an innings and 103 runs before securing a 194-run triumph at Lord’s. Pakistan’s poor performances have since triggered a major overhaul of the national setup.
Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul have departed the coaching setup, while Mike Hesson has taken charge of the team with former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke joining him as an assistant.
The PCB has also made a significant call on the playing group, removing seven players from the squad for the third and final Test. Among those sent back are senior names such as Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha, with the board seemingly turning its attention towards a younger generation.
Shoaib Akhtar explains PCB's thinking
Former Pakistan fast bowler Shoaib Akhtar has now offered his assessment of the dramatic changes, claiming the PCB has effectively lost confidence in a large part of the existing squad.
Speaking on the OutSide EDGE show, Akhtar suggested that the board is no longer simply reacting to the England defeats but is instead using the tour as an opportunity to accelerate a wider rebuilding process.
“The PCB itself was very disappointed by these people, and they don’t expect anything from this Pakistan squad. The plan is to remove this squad and replace them with younger and newer blood. Players who just want to play for Pakistan. They are looking at the future now, and they are working at it in the right way,” Akhtar said.
The former pacer, however, stressed that Pakistan must be careful while making such a transition. He specifically named Shaheen Shah Afridi, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf as three players whose careers should be protected as the team undergoes major changes.
“In this transition, I just want Shaheen Shah Afridi, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf’s careers to be saved. These guys have a lot of cricket left in them,” he said.
'Nothing' expected from current Pakistan squad
Akhtar also claimed that a conversation with a PCB official gave him a revealing insight into the board's expectations from the current team.
According to the former Pakistan pacer, he asked the official what the PCB expected from the side during its England tour. The response, he said, was blunt.
“Nothing. We have expectations from the next generation of players that we are preparing for the big stage,” Akhtar quoted the official as saying.
Akhtar further claimed that the same official described the state of Pakistan cricket as being “on a ventilator” and believed it could take around two years to revive the national setup.
The comments underline the scale of the challenge facing the PCB, particularly after Pakistan's inability to put up a strong fight in either of the first two Tests.
Akhtar questions Pakistan's lack of fight
The 51-year-old also spoke about what he saw during his visit to the National Cricket Academy in Lahore. Akhtar said he was there during the second Test and noticed considerable infrastructure work taking place.
“After 26 years, there is work being done at the academy now,” Akhtar said.
Despite the upheaval surrounding the senior team, Akhtar suggested that the developments should not have come as a surprise.
When asked whether the turmoil had shocked him, he responded: “What is the shock there? Didn’t you expect that?”
He was equally critical when Pakistan's struggles against England were discussed. Reflecting on the two heavy defeats, Akhtar summed up the team's performances in stark terms.
“We didn’t have the fight in us,” he said.
Pakistan will now travel to Edgbaston for the third Test, where they will attempt to prevent England from completing a 3-0 series whitewash. However, the decisions taken by the PCB before the series has even ended suggest that the problems confronting Pakistan cricket are being viewed as much bigger than the outcome of this England tour.

stories.headline: 'They're clearly hoping to kill him in there': Imran Khan's sons raise serious concerns
stories.deck: The sons of former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan have strongly criticised Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi after the board was accused of threatening to abandon the Lord’s Test against England. Sulaiman and Kasim Khan also raised serious concerns about their father's health and conditions in prison, claiming that Pakistan authorities are trying to silence him.
stories.bodyText:
The sons of former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister 
Imran Khan
 have strongly criticised Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi after the board was accused of threatening to abandon the Lord’s Test against England. Sulaiman and Kasim Khan also raised serious concerns about their father's health and conditions in prison, claiming that Pakistan authorities are trying to silence him.
The controversy began during the second Test at Lord’s after Sky Sports aired an interview conducted by former England captain Michael Atherton with Sulaiman and Kasim.
They spoke about their father's health and his conditions in prison.
Reports later claimed that the PCB threatened not to send the Pakistan team out for the post-lunch session on the first day unless the interview was taken off air.
‘They're clearly hoping to kill him in there’
With Mohsin Naqvi facing increased scrutiny, the sons also spoke about their concerns over Khan's solitary confinement.
Kasim made a serious allegation about the former Pakistan captain's safety.
“They're clearly hoping to kill him in there. They want to silence him as secretly as possible and just slowly make him fade into nothing.
“That's a very difficult thing to do with the most popular person in Pakistan right now. 
Their strategy, whenever we speak, is to let everything fizzle out and then impose more brutal restrictions that make it even harder for him to survive.”
‘They made absolute fools of themselves’
Kasim criticised the PCB's reported reaction and said the board had damaged its own image.
“They made absolute fools of themselves,” Kasim told The Telegraph on Sunday.
Sulaiman said he was surprised that the PCB reacted so strongly to an interview about his father.
“I was expecting some sort of response. But I didn't think they would be so tactless as to threaten not to take to the field.
“It shouldn't be in the remit of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) to ask for an interview about an ex-Pakistan player, somebody who lived in England for 22 years, to be taken down. This wasn't about politics, but about the humanitarian situation and his health.”
Authorities deny mistreatment claims
Pakistani authorities have repeatedly denied allegations of mistreatment and have maintained that Khan is receiving proper medical care.
Sulaiman, however, questioned those assurances and said the family had not been given enough information about his father's condition.
“The worrying theory we're hearing is that they're drip-feeding these reports of his ailing health and pretending that they're trying to help him, just to lay the ground for something worse to happen. Then they can wash their hands and say: 'He's just an old man who died, and we had nothing to do with it.’
“They haven't given us proof of any of this. It's all just hearsay from government sources – there's no transparency, they don't want to give anyone access, so how are we supposed to believe any of it? The last verifiable piece of information we had was from him, six months ago, when he spoke about his eye and how it had been neglected.”

briefs.headline: Karnataka farmers oppose move to acquire land for Dharwad–Belagavi industrial corridor
briefs.deck: Farmers oppose move to acquire land for industrial corridor
briefs.bodyText: Dharwad: Farmers in Hosaval, Veerapur, Ramapur, Heggeri and surrounding villages in the taluk have opposed the government’s move to acquire their land for the Dharwad–Belagavi industrial corridor under the Suvarna Karnataka project..The government has issued a notification to acquire around 6,000 acres..Farmers allege that around 270 acres of land where they have been cultivating both kharif and rabi crops for generations has been classified as 'B kharab' land in their title deeds. 'B kharab' is land classified as uncultivable and vested entirely with the government. Private individuals cannot legally transact such land..The move has triggered opposition from a section of farmers, who say they will not part with their land under any circumstances. They have been staging a protest for the past 5 days..Centre sets lower paddy procurement target of 708.64 lakh tonne for Kharif marketing season 2026-27.Farmer leaders Uday Kumar and Mohammad Ali said the land was highly fertile.."The land is located adjacent to a forest. Acquiring it for industrial purposes will not only deprive farmers of their livelihood, but also push them to the streets," they said..The farmers questioned the change in the classification of land that, according to them, had been granted to them under the 'tiller is the owner' scheme in 1980..All lands in these villages are irrigation-dependent and are used to grow sugarcane, green gram, maize, vegetables and horticulture crops. Farmers also cultivate commercial crops like cotton and soybean. .The farmers have also opposed the compensation fixed by the government, at Rs 45 lakh per acre. ."If the government is determined to acquire our land, it should offer at least Rs 1 crore per acre," the protesting farmers said.

briefs.headline: 'Bengaluru is a global city, 2 lakh foreign passport holders work here': DK Shivakumar

briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Sunday hailed Bengaluru's human resource capacity, noting that the state capital had 26 lakh IT professionals, as against 16 lakh in California's Silicon Valley..Speaking during the Study Abroad 2026 programme, the chief minister said: "Bengaluru is a global city. As many as 2 lakh foreign passport holders work here. If there are 16 lakh IT professionals in California's Silicon Valley, there are 26 lakh IT professionals in Bengaluru. Each year over 1 lakh engineers and 13,940 doctors are being produced, and human resource of this extent is not created anywhere else.".Claiming that the 'talented human resource' being created in Karnataka was not present in any other state in the country, the chief minister said: "Our children should learn at the global level. They should not just get jobs but become job-givers. That's our wish.".Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar urges students to study abroad, become job creators.Appreciating Skill Development Minister Sharan Prakash Patil, Shivakumar said the investment in knowledge would become a property for everyone..Noting that over 80 universities had participated in the event, he explained that opportunities to study over 300 subjects had been created.."Alongside, various departments of the government are providing special scholarships. With different banks providing help, we are providing loan opportunities till Rs 2 crore. Students of the state should utilise it and get stronger and shape a bright future."

stories.headline: Machete attack: Man assaulted for mediating family dispute in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: A man who had stepped in to settle a family dispute was attacked with a machete in full public view in Shabarinagar, under the jurisdiction of Kothanur police station, Saturday night.
The incident took place around 9pm, with the entire attack captured on CCTV cameras.
A dispute had earlier broken out between the families of a brother and sister during a function, following a bike theft case registered at Sampigehalli police station, and the bike was recovered by police. Syed Iliyas Pasha had intervened and tried to pacify both sides. However, the dispute continued even after his intervention, eventually leading to complaints and counter-complaints being filed at Kothanur police station in Aug.
Angered by the registration of FIRs, the accused, 
Salman
, 28, who works in Dubai and is a brother of the man accused of stealing the bike, came to Bengaluru and targeted Pasha on Saturday around 9 pm. Salman attacked him with a machete, leaving him with a serious injury to his abdomen, and escaped.
Pasha was immediately rushed to a private hospital, where he is undergoing treatment. A senior officer said, “Salman is at large. We suspect that he has taken a flight to Dubai on the same night, and efforts are on to nab him.”

stories.headline: SIR: Amid pressure, Karnataka CEO makes SIR notice list public
stories.bodyText:
After sustained public pressure, with several people reporting that they had received notices at the last minute, leaving them with a narrow window to respond, the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) has made the notice list public.
A total of 43.81 lakh people across the State have been marked to receive notices.
The list can be accessed here: https://ceo.karnataka.gov.in/notices_issued.html
It does not specify the hearing venue, date or time. This leaves voters in the dark about when and where they are expected to appear, adding to the confusion and burden surrounding an already opaque process.
With hearings having begun on Thursday across Karnataka, the situation has left many people with no option but to miss their hearings because of the short notice and lack of prior information. The public can now access the list, with district-wise files uploaded on the website, similar to the ASDDO list.
While the list has been made public, it only indicates that a person has been marked for a notice. It does not specify the hearing venue, date or time. This leaves voters in the dark about when and where they are expected to appear, adding to the confusion and burden surrounding an already opaque process.
The major hurdle flagged by electors is that only the person issued the notice can appear for the hearing, and no one else can represent the voter at the hearing venue. Moreover, a hearing can be rescheduled only once, at the discretion of the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO).
Electors have also flagged that Booth Level Officers (BLOs) are not visiting voters’ homes to serve notices, but are instead asking them to collect the notices from the polling station, citing their duties at hearing venues. However, the hearings are to be conducted by the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) or Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), not the BLOs.
Notices have been issued for two broad reasons: non-mapping, where a voter could not map their own or their parent’s details to the 2002 electoral rolls, and anomalies or “logical discrepancies”, such as an implausible age gap between an elector and their parents or grandparents, differences in the spelling of the father’s name, or a mismatch in the voter’s own name in cases of self-mapping.
However, while these are the stated reasons for generating notices, several people in Bengaluru have reported receiving notices despite having filled in all their details correctly.
Even where a voter has correctly provided all the required details and there is no actual logical discrepancy or mapping gap, being wrongly issued a notice does not spare them the inquiry. Recently, in Byatarayanapura, the Bengaluru DEO found that three people had been issued notices despite the mapping details they had provided being correct. Yet, the order still required them to appear for an inquiry. The entire burden continues to fall on the voter, even when the error is not theirs.

stories.headline: Krishna Byre Gowda pulls up absent pourakarmikas of Bengaluru: ‘First work, then seek regularisation’
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Around 30% of Bengaluru’s pourakarmikas were found absent during a surprise early-morning inspection by Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda Saturday, prompting him to publicly reprimand the workers demanding job regularisation.
In a video that has since gone viral on social media, he is seen interacting with pourakarmikas. The minister is heard telling the workers that they must first report to work regularly and perform their duties before demanding permanent employment.
He pointed out that their absenteeism was affecting cleanliness across the city and resulting in public criticism of the govt and civic authorities.
Bengaluru has around 16,000 pourakarmikas, of whom about 12,800 have already been regularised. The remaining workers are yet to be absorbed into govt service. Auto drivers and helpers, meanwhile, continue to work under private contracts.
Sunday, All-India Central Council of Trade Unions (AICCTU) demanded an apology from the minister, alleging that he had publicly humiliated civic workers, many of whom are women and dalits. It condemned what it called the minister’s “insulting and degrading” attitude towards pourakarmikas, saying the workers were on the frontline of maintaining the city’s cleanliness and public health.
AICCTU said the minister’s remarks ignored the larger issues faced by pourakarmikas, including the contract and outsourcing system, work pressure, delayed wages, lack of safety equipment and inadequate social security. “Efficiency does not mean scolding the workers but managing the city in a scientific and humane manner while maintaining the rights, dignity and security of the workers,” the union said.
It also demanded weekly offs for the workers and an end to the contract and outsourcing system.
Box
Biocon founder backs minister amid online debate
The minister’s remarks triggered discussion online, with several people supporting his stance and others questioning whether the working conditions of pourakarmikas had received adequate attention.
Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw praised Byre Gowda’s intervention. “Well said, Krishna Byre Gowda, our pourakarmikas need to first demonstrate responsible workmanship. Unless the city is clean, no question of permanent jobs,” she wrote on X.
Several other social media users echoed similar sentiments. User ThirdEye wrote: “KBG is spitting facts here. Most of the pourakarmikas demand money from each house/apartment to collect garbage. If you don’t pay them, they just don’t turn up every morning.”
Another user, RSNMurthy, wrote: “Very true. Many can be seen in clean uniform roaming on scooters with brooms in Malleswaram when few dedicated men work hard to keep the area clean.”
Prakash Naik wrote: “Sometimes garbage is filled on footpaths for a week in JP Nagar 8th phase, no accountability. Thanks for questioning and bringing some discipline.”
However, many others posted in support of the civic workers. Clifton D’ Rozario, replying to Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw’s post, wrote, “Publicly humiliating Dalit Pourakarmikas in a democracy is “Well Said”! Feudal minds do think alike. Garbage vehicle workers are exploited under the contract system – not paid for months. No ESI/PF/Weekly off/ water/toilets while they are handling rotting garbage with bare hands.”
Krushika AV wrote, “Making their employment permanent is their right. You are no king, minister. They aren’t your subjects. Making their employment permanent ensures rights & benefits. You aren’t doing any favous…”
SrinivasHande wrote, “@krishnabyregowda this is unacceptable. Do you know they ain’t provided with even basic gears to protect themselves. There is no dignity in pourakarmikas’ job. They are treated badly even though they are single most important people to sustain a city like Bengaluru. Have respect.”

stories.headline: Karnataka files appeal before CWMA seeking reduction in water release
stories.deck: Appeal comes ahead of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee meeting scheduled on September 8
stories.bodyText:
Ahead of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) meeting scheduled this week, Karnataka has filed an appeal before the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) seeking a reduction in water release to Tamil Nadu from 9,000 cusecs a day, as ordered by it, to 2,000 cusecs.
It may be noted that the CWMA had upheld the CWRC’s August 25 direction to Karnataka, asking it to ensure flows of 9,000 cusecs a day for 15 days from August 25 to be realised at the Biligundlu water gauge on the inter-State border. According to the CWMA’s order, the releases by Karnataka would total up to 11.66 tmcft.
The CWRC is meeting again on September 8 to review the ground-level situation. On the same day, the CWMA is also meeting to review the situation.
Meanwhile, Karnataka has filed an appeal before the CWMA seeking a reduction in water release on the grounds that the inflows into its Cauvery reservoirs are very low. It has also pointed out that the southwest Monsoon is set to end soon, indicating that there is no hope for the State that there will be further inflows into its Cauvery reservoirs in the future.
It may be noted that Karnataka, on August 25, had appealed to the CWMA to adopt a cautious approach while asking for any further release, and requested the Authority to reassess the situation after observing the forthcoming northeast monsoon. The State had told the CWMA that its Cauvery basin area was facing severe hydrological distress, due to which cumulative inflows into its four reservoirs in the Cauvery basin were about 49.18% below the 30-year average.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru's warmth sets it apart: British Diplomat Chandru Iyer
briefs.deck: As he completes his four-year tenure as British Deputy High Commissioner for Karnataka, Chandru Iyer reflects on the people, food, culture and experiences that have made Bengaluru and the state feel like home
briefs.bodyText:
Savouring one of his last masala dosaes in Bengaluru, just a day before completing his tenure as British Deputy High Commissioner for Karnataka, Chandru Iyer sits down with Bangalore Times to reflect on the city and state that have been home to him for four years. The rakhis still adorning his wrist — some sent by his sisters and others tied by family in Bengaluru — are a reminder of the personal connections he has made here. But as he looks back on his time in Karnataka, it is the people, culture, art, food and distinctive character of the state that dominate his reflections. Having travelled extensively across Karnataka during his tenure, Chandru says what stands out most is its diversity — not just in its landscapes and cuisine, but also in the way its communities coexist. Excerpts:
‘There’s so much to see and do in Karnataka’
His experience of Karnataka extends well beyond Bengaluru. Over the past four years, Chandru has travelled to Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Davangere, Belagavi, Dakshina Kannada, Chikkamagaluru and Kodagu, among other places. “I think if you want to understand a state or a region, you need to go around,” he says. “There’s so much to do here and so much to see. We’ve got Hampi, the Western Ghats, temples, forts, waterfalls and Jog Falls. I think it’s time that we take the Karnataka story to the world,” he reflects.
‘Can we have a Karnataka festival at Trafalgar Square?’
For Chandru, the next step is taking Karnataka’s diversity beyond the state and even beyond India. He hopes to see a festival in London that showcases Karnataka’s food, culture, traditions, crafts and products. “My vision is to get Mysore sandal soap, Mysore silk, Chikkamagaluru coffee and Channapatna toys to the UK. We can celebrate the food, culture, traditions and people of Karnataka,” he says.
One of the easiest ways to experience Karnataka, Chandru says, is through its food. His travels across the state have introduced him to Davangere benne dose, Hubballi-Dharwad’s susla, Mysuru’s Mylari dosa, Mangaluru buns and goli bajji. “Mangaluru is also the ice cream capital of the country. It’s amazing to see the quality of ice cream brands there. I’m keen to see if some of these brands can come and set up outlets in the UK. That’ll be fun,” he says.
‘People coming together and living together is what defines Bengaluru’
Living near Ulsoor Lake gave Chandru a particularly intimate view of Bengaluru. His mornings brought together sounds, sights and experiences that, for him, captured the essence of the city. “Every morning, I wake up to the view of the lake and its greenery and the modern skyline. I hear the Shabad Kirtan from the nearby Gurudwara and smell the kada prasad. I can hear the bells from Someshwara Temple and the azaan from the mosque. I think that’s what really defines India, Karnataka and Bengaluru — people coming together and living together,” he says.
For him, this spirit of coexistence is one of Bengaluru’s defining characteristics. “The warmth of the people is what sets this city apart from some of the other global cities,” he says. He also believes Bengaluru’s green spaces remain central to its identity, even as the city continues to grow and its weather changes.
“I think it is still one of the greenest cities in India. I love the weather. There are a few months when it’s hot, but post-summer, it’s beautiful. When I come out of my house, have a cup of South Indian filter coffee and look at the skyline, I think no other metro city in India has what Bengaluru has.”
Ultimately, however, it is the everyday Bengaluru experience that appears to have left the strongest impression on Chandru. “I’ve made friends for life here,” he says. “Sometimes, with diplomatic postings, you move from one city to another and you forget people. But this city has been such that I don’t think they will allow me to forget them.”

briefs.headline: Power shock at 11 kV line: 2 Bescom workers injured in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Two Bescom workers sustained electric shocks while attending an 11 kV jump cut near Sahasra Hospital on Varthur Main Road between 10.30am and 11am, allegedly due to back-feeding from a diesel generator.
Venkataraju, 46, and 
Srinivas
, 47, were attending the fault near a Gang Operated Switch structure when they were electrocuted. They had climbed the structure using a wooden ladder while responding to a complaint. The duo were initially taken to Sahasra Hospital and later shifted to a private hospital on Old Airport Road. Both are stable.
Varthur police said the workers were found unconscious on the structure, following which Bescom was alerted and power supply was disconnected. No official complaint has been registered.
Power line fire in RT Nagar
Panic gripped RT Nagar Saturday evening after a short circuit triggered a fire on a power line near an online grocery warehouse at 6pm. Locals reported flames and an explosion before alerting Bescom. Personnel inspected the affected line. No casualties were reported.

briefs.headline: Vehicles parked outside Bengaluru house catch fire
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Several vehicles parked in the compound of a house were gutted in a midnight fire near Cambridge School in Doddanagamangala, under Parappana Agrahara police limits, Saturday.
The two-wheelers, parked by tenants in the residential building’s parking area, caught fire at 1am. The flames spread to the house, damaging the electric meter board, doors and windows.
Residents were left puzzled after another motorcycle parked some distance away also caught fire, raising suspicion over whether the blaze was accidental or deliberately set.
Parappana Agrahara police have registered a case. The exact cause of the fire is yet to be established.

briefs.headline: Modified silencer lands Bengaluru biker with challan of Rs 500
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: “Style” shouldn’t come at the cost of someone else’s peace of mind. Taking a strict stand against noise pollution, HAL Airport traffic police have warned motorists using modified exhausts of severe action.
As part of the crackdown, police Saturday caught a biker riding with a defective silencer and imposed a Rs 500 fine on him. The rider had reportedly been captured by a member of the public while riding in Vignananagar on Aug 18. Acting on the X post, HAL traffic police traced the biker and initiated action against him.
During questioning, the rider, who works at a market in HAL, reportedly told police that he had purchased the bike from another person a few months ago. He claimed that the previous owner had modified the silencer.
Police said they would continue their drive against modified exhausts and defective silencers.

briefs.headline: Karnataka FDA seizes drugs worth ₹4 lakh from illegal storage
briefs.bodyText:
The Drugs Enforcement Wing of the Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) raided unlicensed e-commerce storage facilities and seized large stocks of unauthorised medicines on Sunday.
According to details shared by officials, the crackdown on the illegal storage and distribution of pharmaceuticals happened following precise intelligence information regarding major compliance breaches.
While one team led by Manohar, Assistant Drugs Controller (ADC) from the State Intelligence Branch, raided a unit in Anekal, another team led by Vibha, Drugs Inspector, Bangalore Rural, raided another unit in Devanahalli.
Mr. Manohar, along with other drugs inspectors, raided the unlicensed premises of Amazon Seller Services Private Limited located in Thattanahalli, Anekal taluk, and seized medicines worth ₹2,45,352. These medicines were being stored without a valid drug license.
At the same time, the team in Devanahalli seized illegally stored medicines worth ₹1,57,000 from another unlicensed facility of Amazon at Aerospace Park.

briefs.headline: Clay or PoP? Bengaluru’s Ganesha idol makers, sellers face uneasy choice
briefs.bodyText:
While the State government, NGOs, and environmental activists are encouraging people to purchase eco-friendly Ganeshas for the upcoming Ganesh Chaturthi festival, idol makers and sellers say that people still prefer buying coloured Ganeshas for celebrations at home and Plaster of Paris (PoP) Ganeshas for pandal celebrations.
The Hindu visited some of the places in the city, including Pottery Town, Mavalli, and Seshadripuram, where Ganesha idols have been prepared, displayed, and sold in large numbers for more than five decades.
Shashikumar, a fourth-generation member of the Kumbara community involved in selling Ganesha idols at Pottery Town, said, “Earlier, our family used to prepare Ganesha idols, but due to space constraints as well as a lack of availability of clay and skilled labour, I now buy idols from makers in Hosur. While I understand that PoP idols are harmful to the environment, many customers prefer buying them, and at the same time, idol makers invest crores in making them.”
He added, “If the government has to create awareness and stop PoP idols from coming into the market, then they must start creating awareness as early as November, almost immediately after the festival. It is at this time that makers invest money in materials and labour to make idols. Creating awareness at the last minute doesn’t help, as these idols would have already entered the market.”
Mr. Shashikumar also said that one cannot make idols as huge as six to 12 feet using clay. “They turn out to be heavy, making them difficult to lift, and structuring them is a challenge. Hence, all large idols are made of PoP and paper.”
Making PoP idols is easy
Mr. Shashikumar further said that making PoP idols is easier than making idols from clay. He explained, “The materials used in PoP help the idols mould easily with designs and shapes, and they dry within six hours. The colours can also be sprayed immediately. Meanwhile, clay idols have to be prepared three months in advance so that they dry well to be painted later.”
Meanwhile, Govardhan, another member of the Kumbara community, said, “There are fewer families who prefer to buy handmade, eco-friendly idols from our shops compared to those who order the moulded and coloured ones. There are only 200 such families traditionally buying clay idols from my shop. If I make a larger number of eco-friendly idols, I will suffer a loss. Hence, there are more coloured idols than handmade and plain ones.”
Mr. Govardhan added, “Sourcing clay is another challenge for idol makers. Earlier, it was available to us in and around the city lakes. With the number of lakes reduced, there is no soil, and we are forced to buy it from Bagalur Road, Hoskote, etc. A small load of clay costs ₹12,000.”
When asked about the type of colours used in painting Ganesha idols, he said, “These are not harmful ones. Earlier, we used oil paint, but that was poisonous to water bodies. Now, we use water paint, which is chemical-free.”
However, Nandeesh from Bettahalsuru, who is exclusively into making eco-friendly idols, said, “Idol makers claim that these water paints are not harmful. But they do contain chemicals and leave residue in water. In order to protect water bodies from pollution, I do my bit by making plain clay idols. The prices for plain ones are supposed to be higher in comparison to the coloured ones; however, the prices for our idols range from ₹50 to ₹500. I limit myself to making only 1.5-foot idols.”
Special Operation Team to prevent sale of PoP idols
Bengaluru: Minister for Forest, Ecology, and Environment Ramalinga Reddy has announced a Special Operation Team to prevent the manufacturing and sale of PoP Ganesha idols that harm the environment. They will be assisted by the local police and other departments, he noted.
He also said that the team inspected 214 shops and warehouses in Shivamogga, Tumakuru, Bagalkot, Haveri, Gadag, Dharwad, Kalaburagi, Bidar, Yadgir, Ballari, Koppal, Raichur, and Vijayanagara districts, where they were being manufactured without following the guidelines, and 1,283 such idols were confiscated. He urged the general public to purchase eco-friendly idols for the festival and save lakes.

briefs.headline: London-bound plane makes ‘emergency landing’ at Bengaluru airport after technical snag
briefs.deck: The flight took off from KIAB at around 8.20 a.m. but reportedly developed a technical issue soon after departure, prompting the crew to circle the aircraft near Tumakuru for more than half an hour before returning to Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
A London-bound Virgin Atlantic flight carrying 270 passengers was forced to make an "emergency landing" at the Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru on Sunday (September 6, 2026) after developing a technical glitch shortly after take-off, sources at Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL), which operates KIAB, said.
The flight took off from KIAB at around 8.20 a.m. but reportedly developed a technical issue soon after departure, prompting the crew to circle the aircraft near Tumakuru for more than half an hour before returning to Bengaluru.
“All passengers on board are safe,” sources at BIAL said, adding that the aircraft was brought back to KIAB as a safety precaution and made an emergency landing.
The exact nature of the technical problem was not immediately known. Authorities are looking into the cause of the incident.
However, there was no immediate reaction from the airlines.
The flight was carrying approximately 270 passengers bound for London.

briefs.headline: SIR hearings descend into confusion and chaos on Day 1 in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: While some voters had come to collect their notices, many did not know what a “logical discrepancy” meant, why their name had been marked as “not mapped” or what they were expected to prove.
briefs.bodyText:
On the first day of hearing for voters in Bengaluru under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), some questions were commonly heard in the single-room offices of Booth Level Officers (BLOs) across multiple centres — “Can you give me my notice?”, “Is my name there?”, “What documents do I have to show?”...
While some had come to collect their notices, many did not know what a “logical discrepancy” meant or why their name had been marked as “not mapped” or what they were expected to prove.
At a BBMP ward office in C.V. Raman Nagar constituency, 82-year-old wheelchair-bound Selva Raj had arrived with three photocopies each of his Aadhaar and ration card. He had assumed these documents would help establish that he had been living in and voting from the same constituency, against his notice flagged for “no mapping”. Mr. Selva Raj did not know that they were not among the 11 accepted documents.
“This is no less than mental harassment,” he said, pointing to the wheelchair.
The hearing across the city left voters — particularly the elderly who struggled to reach the venue and those who were clueless about the process — scrambling to understand what they had to do, and exposed the lack of awareness among the public.
At hearing venues in C.V. Raman Nagar, Cox Town and parts of Central Bengaluru visited by The Hindu, people and BLOs were equally anxious and confused.
Within the small space occupied by at least 100 voters at Cox Town BBMP ward office, people were pushing past each other to find their names on the list of voters issued notices and show them to their BLO. Many did not know that they first had to establish that their name was on the list before approaching the BLO.
At another venue in Cox Town, the BLO was left scanning notices while also trying to locate the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) who was supposed to conduct the hearings. The AERO was nowhere to be found as voters waited. At another venue in the same area, an AERO himself was seen struggling with the scanning process.
Many voters, like Samar Halarnkar, a resident of Richards Town, could not even get a copy of their notice amid the overwhelming crowd. Mr. Halarnkar and his 90-year-old mother had received notices for a hearing later this month. Like many others, he thought that the process was over and that their names were secure because they appeared in the draft rolls.
However, he learnt about the notice through a WhatsApp group and had to go himself to get a copy, though the process states that BLOs should serve the notice and click and upload a photograph of it.
The college where the two are expected to appear for the hearing is at the end of a dug-up lane accessible only by two-wheelers, he said, arguing that there was no chance his 90-year-old, wheelchair-bound mother could get there.
No idea about documents
Much like during the enumeration phase, confusion over documents persisted. Many voters said they had no idea which documents to carry. “We thought the process would be similar to enumeration, but this time only physical verification would be done, where BLOs would check the form and ask for Aadhaar, PAN or ration card,” David, a voter from Indiranagar, said.
Many voters the The Hindu met said they did not have birth certificates, let alone passports. Several women said they had no documents, including Aadhaar.
Senior journalist T.M. Veera Raghav, who accompanied a family member to a hearing venue in Kengeri, described the process as cumbersome and said that if done this way, it would result in many people missing out on the hearings. While BLOs were helpful, he said, many people did not even know why they had been served notices, as the notices were only in Kannada.
Karnataka CEO V. Anbu Kumar had said that notices would be served in Kannada and one more language as per regional need — English and Kannada for Bengaluru and Marathi and Kannada for Belagavi, for instance. However, voters have so far received notices only in Kannada.

stories.headline: China to pump $54 billion into state banks, insurers
stories.bodyText:
BEIJING: China's finance ministry will lead a combined $54 billion in capital injections into state-owned insurers and banks, the companies said on Sunday, in a coordinated push by Beijing to shore up capital across its financial system.
China Life Insurance (Group) Co, the country's largest life insurer, will receive $5.2 billion, while China Taiping Insurance Group will get about $1 billion, the two groups said in statements.
Separately, People's Insurance Company (Group) of China said it planned to raise up to $2.2 billion through a private placement of A-shares to ministry of finance, with the proceeds to be used to replenish its capital. The initiative could help bolster state insurers that were directed to support the stock market with medium- and long-term funds, while positioning them to help regulators manage smaller, higher-risk insurance companies.
The insurance sector has been grappling with eroding profitability due to persistently low interest rates, with numerous small and mid-sized insurers reporting deteriorating solvency ratios.
China Export and Credit Insurance Corp also said the finance ministry will inject about $1.5 billion to boost its core capital, and China Reinsurance (Group) said it will raise $447 million. "The injection is an important step by the country to enhance the financial sector's ability to serve the real economy and promote the high-quality development of the financial and insurance industries," China Life said in its statement, adding that it would strengthen the group's ability to withstand risks.
Taiping said the funds would bolster its solvency and other key indicators. Separately, three state lenders announced they will receive a total of $43 billion in capital infusion.
(This is a Reuters story)

stories.headline: Busy week ahead: Companies set to raise Rs 7.2k crore via IPOs
stories.deck: D-St Warms Up In Build-Up To Mega NSE, Jio Platforms Offers
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The new week promises to be extremely busy for the primary market with as many as 11 main board and five SME offers lined up, together targeting about Rs 7,200 crore. This is a precursor to the likely blockbuster later in the month when NSE IPO opens to raise an estimated Rs 30,000 crore. A few weeks down the line, Dalal Street is expected to see another mega offer, that of Jio Platforms eyeing about Rs 37,000 crore.
As things stand, when NSE IPO closes in about two weeks from now, it would be the biggest primary offer in India, ahead of the Rs 27,800 crore offer from Hyundai Motors India that had closed in late 2024. However, that ranking will change after Jio Platforms lists at end-Oct or early-Nov.
During the current week, the IPO rush is being led by RentoMojo, which is eyeing Rs 1,256 crore from investors. The offer, a combination of a fresh issue worth Rs 150 crore and another offer for sale worth Rs 1,106 crore, is set to open on Sept 9 and close on Sept 11, data from public offer analytics platform Chittorgarh showed.
The week is also set to witness the launch of an offer from a company that's a new category for Dalal Street: ARCIL, the first asset reconstruction company to be set up in India, is tapping the market for a Rs 733 crore offer. 
The IPO will open on Sept 9 and close on Sept 11.
The IPO week will kick off on Monday itself with the Rs 515 crore offer for Pranav Constructions. It will close on Wednesday. Three issues: Glass Wall Systems' Rs 428 crore offer, Prasol Chemicals' Rs 500 crore offer and Kanohar Electricals' Rs 1,056 crore offer will open on Sept 8 and close on Sept 10.
The other large offers that would go live during the week are Manipal Payment and Identity Solutions (Rs 805 crore offer), Steamhouse India (Rs 414 crore), LCC Projects (Rs 427 crore) and Karamtara Engineering (Rs 875 crore). In addition to these issues, there are also three companies that are slotted to list on the main boards of the bourses: Purple Style Labs, Rays of Belief and Deepa Jewellers.

stories.headline: India’s unemployment data dilemma
stories.deck: A fall in unemployment may indicate distress-driven entry into low-productivity jobs rather than genuine employment creation
stories.bodyText:
The government has finally found a way to measure the statistical elephant of unemployment; however, it may be incomplete — much like the blind men who touched different parts of a pachyderm and mistook it for the whole truth.
The challenge in measuring the unemployment rate using the Current Weekly Status (CWS) approach — where a person’s activity status is determined based on the preceding seven days — is to assess not only whether people are employed, but also the nature of their jobs, the frequency and regularity of their payments, and the overall quality of employment. In an economy where a vast majority of the population are involved in informal work, employment cannot be analysed through a headline rate of high frequency indicator, if it can be called so.
Also Read | Marginal increase in unemployment rate April-June quarter: PLFS
India’s decision to transform the quarterly/yearly unemployment data into a monthly indicator is economically desirable, even if its credibility is questionable given the nature of its database, which seldom takes into account circular migration.
Efforts have been made to strengthen India’s database comprising EPFO (Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation) and ESIC (Employees’ State Insurance Corporation) payroll data, GST-based enterprise information, income tax records, corporate payroll data, gig economy employment data, and rural wage indicators but at present, even these sources remain fragmented. Unlike a mature labour market — comprising payroll surveys, unemployment insurance records, formal contracts, and extensive administrative databases — India’s large informal employment market is difficult to track.
Most advanced nations count unemployment using a Labour Force Survey based on the definition of the International Labour Organization (ILO). The U.S., Japan, EU and the U.K. have decades of household survey data with detailed information on full-time versus part-time jobs, hourly wages, job duration, labour mobility, and unemployment spells.
Also Read | The stark reality of the missing jobs for India’s Gen Z
A leading indicator
The latest Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) says that India’s unemployment rate for those aged 15 years and above marked a four-month low of 5.1% in July. The review period coincided with the peak of kharif season, when demand for agricultural labour rose for land preparation, transplanting, and allied activities. Since construction, agriculture, small trade, logistics, and local services see seasonal fluctuations, it is likely that July’s decline reflects increased hiring in these segments rather than a broad-based expansion in formal sector jobs.
Monthly unemployment should at the best be a leading indicator, not a comprehensive measure of labour market health.
India has a labour market where various reports suggest that 90% of the population are involved in the informal sector; agricultural employment remains seasonal, with wage payments negotiated informally and where underemployment/ disguised employment is widespread. Indicating limited granularity, data is rather sketchy on wage growth, hours worked, job quality, occupational shifts, and sector-wise employment trends. Therefore, monthly unemployment data reflects seasonal movements rather than structural improvement. A fall in unemployment may indicate distress-driven entry into low-productivity jobs rather than genuine employment creation.
COMMENT | The fact is youth unemployment has a household cost
The overall decline in unemployment was owing to rural areas, where unemployment declined to 4.5% from 5%; but it should not be read as a major improvement in the job market. Independent labour studies estimate that there are between 30 to 35 million seasonal labourers moving across India annually, forming the invisible backbone of urban construction and infrastructure.
The July data saw an increase in the labour force participation rate, a positive supply-side signal, but stronger investment and job creation prefix sustainable employment recovery. The challenge is to convert this participation into stable, high-productivity jobs.
The revamped PLFS is a significant improvement over earlier low-frequency labour statistics but its success ultimately depends on whether it gauges the reality of the job market — not merely measuring it more frequently. A credible labour market barometer is the need of the hour to capture the livelihoods of millions of workers.

stories.headline: Gold and silver rise
stories.deck: Short-term trend in gold and silver have turned positive post the breakout of key resistance level; the trend would remain positive until the support level is breached
stories.bodyText:
Breaking the downtrend of several months, precious metals recovered sharply in August. The expectations around interest rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve played a key role in influencing the prices. The weakening of the U.S. Dollar too helped precious metals stage a recovery in August.
Comex gold gained 9.73 % in August to settle at $4,497.3/ounce by month end. Comex silver posted an even better performance gaining 16.32% to settle at $67.2/ounce.
Gain in local markets
Mirroring global market trend, the precious metal prices settled higher in the local markets too. The gains were, however curtailed by Indian Rupee strengthening against the U.S. Dollar.
MCX Gold gained 7.75% to settle at ₹1,54,456/10 gm. MCX Silver, too, closed on strong note at ₹2,40,250/kg, a 8.46% gain last month.
Comex gold price managed to breakout above the resistance level of $4,410 mentioned last month. In line with last month’s observation, the price later moved to the target zone of $4,650-$4,700. The short-term outlook for gold has turned positive and the price could head to the next target at $4,750-$4,800.
The positive outlook for Comex gold would be under threat only if the price falls below the support at the $4,200-$4,220 zone. Until this zone is breached, expect the gold price to head to the target mentioned above.
Similar to gold, Comex silver price, too, staged a breakout above the resistance level of $66. The short-term outlook as a result has turned positive. The price could now head to the immediate target zone of $72-$74. The positive outlook would be valid as long as the price stays above the support level at $62.5.
MCX gold price, too, crossed above resistance level at ₹1,49,000 and later scaled a high of ₹1,64,773 on August 24 before receding a bit in the past few days. The short-term outlook has turned positive and the price could head to ₹1,66,000-₹1,68,000 zone. The positive outlook would invalidate if the price drops below ₹1,48,000.
Similar to gold, the trend in MCX silver price has turned positive after the price moved past the resistance level of ₹2,45,000. As long as the price stays above ₹2,25,000, the price could move to next target zone of ₹2,56,000-₹2,59,000.
To summarise, the short-term trend in both gold and silver have turned positive post the breakout of key resistance level. The trend would remain positive until the support level mentioned above is breached.
(The author is a Chennai-based analyst/trader. Views, opinions in this column are based on an analysis of short-term price movement in gold and silver futures at COMEX & Multi Commodity Exchange of India. This is not a trading or investment advice.)
